Article Title: 'Much more to this than meets the eye': Rahul targets PM Modi after US court drops case against Adani
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday reacted sharply to Gautam Adani 's acquittal by a US court and targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the development.In a post on X, the leader of opposition in Lok Sabha said, "There is much more to this than meets the eye. A compromised PM was forced to sell India’s interest. India is paying a huge price. "A US federal judge in New York on Monday dismissed the nearly two-year-old criminal case against Adani and the other accused. The US Department of Justice had sought dismissal of the charges, citing six “overlapping bases”, including that the case involved foreign conduct, India had not found “actionable misconduct”, no money had been lost on securities issued and there were “extraordinary proof problems”.The case, filed in November 2024, accused Adani, his nephew Sagar Adani and six others of conspiracy to bribe Indian government officials to secure a solar power contract. The Adani Group had denied the allegations and said its companies and executives had acted in accordance with applicable laws and regulatory requirements.Judge Nicholas Garaufis had earlier questioned the DOJ's decision to drop the case and sought further explanation for the move.The DOJ had argued that the defendants were foreign nationals who had never appeared in the US and were unlikely to do so.Adani, meanwhile, welcomed the court's decision, saying: “Throughout this challenging period, our faith in truth, fairness and the rule of law remained unwavering. My deepest gratitude to those who never lost faith in us, in the system and in India’s capacity for justice,” according to the supplied text.
Article Summary: Congress leader rahul gandhi reacted sharply to gautam adani's acquittal by a us court. He targeted prime minister narendra modi over the development. A us federal judge in new york on monday dismissed the nearly two-year-old criminal case against adani and other accused.

Article Title: Govt condemns vandalism of Indian embassy in Slovenia
Article Text:
Ministry of external affairs said in an official statement that under the Vienna Convention, diplomatic premises are inviolable and must be protected.

NEW DELHI: Condemning the defacement of Indian embassy premises in Slovenia by Khalistan separatists, the govt urged law enforcement authorities elsewhere too to take note of the hateful propaganda and disinformation being spread by such groups.Ministry of external affairs said in an official statement that under the Vienna Convention, diplomatic premises are inviolable and must be protected."We have taken up the matter strongly with Slovenian authorities, both in New Delhi and in Ljubljana so that the perpetrators behind such reprehensible acts are held accountable to the full extent of the law," it said."We also call upon law enforcement authorities elsewhere to take note of the hateful propaganda and disinformation being spread by such groups," it added.In recent years, Indian diplomatic missions have been targeted, vandalised, or defaced with pro-Khalistan slogans and flags in many other countries, including Australia, Canada, UK and the US.
Article Summary: Ministry of external affairs said in an official statement that under the vienna convention, diplomatic premises are inviolable and must be protected. In recent years, indian diplomatic missions have been targeted, vandalised, or defaced with pro-khalistan slogans and flags in many other countries, including australia, canada, uk and us.

Article Title: India move will muddle border talks: China
Article Text:
State-run Global Times quoted Chinese experts as saying India’s move would not alter the legal status of the disputed territory but could complicate future boundary negotiations.

GUWAHATI: China has hit back sharply at India for assigning standard names to 27 geographical locations in Arunachal Pradesh, with the state-run Global Times claiming these areas are in China's 'Zangnan' region - Beijing's term for Arunachal Pradesh and adjoining areas that it claims as part of Tibet Autonomous part.The daily reiterated that Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said at a routine press briefing on April 14 that the Zangnan region is China's territory and "China does not recognise the so-called 'Arunachal Pradesh' illegally set up by India. It is fully within China's sovereign rights for the Chinese govt to issue standard names for some of the places in Zangnan."The reaction came three days after India's Survey of India updated its official map to identify 21 land areas, four passes, a high-altitude glacial lake and a 1962 war hero monument in Arunachal Pradesh, which govt said was an exercise to ensure the "correct identification" of places and enhance public awareness of their geographical and historical significance.Global Times reported on Sunday night that the mapping by India came shortly after the 36th meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on China-India Border Affairs (WMCC), held on Aug 6 in New Delhi, where officials from both sides discussed issues including boundary delimitation, border management and control, mechanism building and cross-border cooperation."India's latest move is essentially an attempt to reinforce its claims over disputed territory and counter China's sovereignty position," Guo Xuetang, a professor at Shanghai International Studies University, said.The latest "war of names" adds another layer to an already complex border dispute, even as both sides seek to keep military and diplomatic channels open.

Article Title: Phuket-Delhi Air India pilot fails 2nd dope test, was high on marijuana
Article Text:
Multiple sources told TOI that the PIC was acting under the influence of psychoactive substances.

What govt is doing

NEW DELHI: Trouble mounted for the pilot-in-command (PIC) of last Tuesday’s badly rattled Phuket-Delhi Air India flight after it emerged that he had failed the confirmatory dope test and was found to have consumed marijuana. Besides, the cabin crew of the flight, AI 2379, has filed a complaint with the airline against the “high” PIC’s onboard behaviour.The pilot also faces criminal action beyond DGCA rules — which require such a pilot to be sent for de-addiction and allow him to resume flying after being certified drug-free.The young co-pilot had to single-handedly steady the aircraft and then land it safely at the destination.An alarmed civil aviation ministry summoned AI’s outgoing CEO Campbell Wilson to express concern about this incident and find out how the airline was dealing with the issue and review its plan to come out of its prolonged period of operational turbulence.The incident that has raised questions over the robustness of the Indian system has also pushed DGCA to explore ways to make dope test rules more stringent after the incident that left 20 passengers and four cabin crew members injured.“Certain records, statements, medical information and other material collected during the investigation are protected and confidential in accordance with the applicable investigation framework….AAIB (Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau) requests all concerned to respect the investigation process and refrain from drawing conclusions… AAIB will conduct a thorough investigation covering all material facts and relevant evidence and will issue its preliminary findings,” the aviation ministry said in a statement while responding to queries on the confirmatory test.Multiple sources told TOI that the PIC was acting under the influence of psychoactive substances. “He was often sitting on the floor of the flight deck and tried to smoke out. Cabin crew had to help him back to his seat. He was not in full control of himself. He was unable to walk properly after exiting the aircraft,” said a person in the know. AI did not comment on the cabin crew’s alleged complaints.The probe will determine whether the aircraft had a sudden loss of altitude due to a series of multiple and rare technical snags, which have been reported by the co-pilot in his report, or it was caused by actions of the PIC.When the aircraft experienced loss of altitude, the PIC is learnt to have been standing and leaning behind the co-pilot’s seat. The Airbus A320 had momentarily gone into a “negative G” situation when the PIC and things in the cockpit floated up and those who were not wearing seat belts got injured in the passenger cabin.Also read: Dope test of turbulent Air India flight’s pilot ‘not negative’, sent for confirmation, says government The cabin crew have given a report to AI. The co-pilot may have informed the airline’s ground control about the pilot’s behaviour due to which the unusual step of subjecting the cockpit crew to a drug test — instead of just breath analyser tests — was taken.“AAIB is engaged in systematic collection, preservation and examination of all relevant technical, operational, medical and human-factor evidence,” the govt said.While DGCA is reviewing its rule titled “procedure for examination of aviation personnel for consumption of psychoactive substances”, India’s senior-most pilots sought a differentiation between a pilot testing positive after having a medication for sleeping or anxiety and those who are found to have consumed “true” psychoactive substances.Airlines have a list of medicines that need to be avoided some hours before flight as they can cause drowsiness.Massive financial losses apart, the airline’s operations and training are again under a cloud, just when it was trying to regain public faith following the Ahmedabad crash in June 2025.While Tatas and partner Singapore Airlines have pumped in thousands of crores and there have been significant cosmetic improvements, it is still looking for leadership and professional management that can usher in the culture required to fly it out of turbulence.
Article Summary: Multiple sources told toi that the pic was acting under the influence of psychoactive substances. The cabin crew of the flight, ai 2379, has filed a complaint with the airline against the “high’ pic’s onboard behaviour. The pilot also faces criminal action beyond dgca rules.

Article Title: Air India Phuket flight probe: Marijuana’s legal availability adds to worries of airlines
Article Text:
Unlike simple breath analyser tests for checking if the crew is tipsy, the process of detecting consumption of psychoactive substances is difficult

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The legal availability of marijuana for either medicinal or recreational use in places like Thailand and Amsterdam has made life difficult for airlines flying there. The reason: Unlike simple breath analyser tests for checking if the crew is tipsy, the process of detecting consumption of psychoactive substances is difficult. The only way to deter their consumption by flight crew members, say officials across multiple airlines, is to increase random dope testing, as there substances usually remain present in the body for much longer than alcohol.The concern across airlines globally to check this stems from the fact that operating a flight “under the influence of any psychoactive substance might render (licensed personnel like pilots) unable to safely and properly exercise” perform their duty, as per the International Civil Aviation Organisation.Possibly the most infamous case of this was a US carrier’s off-duty pilot travelling on the jump seat (extra seat behind pilots) in the flight deck trying to shut down the engines. This off-duty pilot had reportedly taken psychedelic mushrooms two days before the incident and hadn’t slept in 48 hours. “This is a challenge globally. Often the tests are not conclusive if taking some medicine leads to detection of psychoactive substances.However, recent consumption of drugs does show up in tests,” said officials.DGCA rules on “procedure for examination of the aviation personnel for consumption of psychoactive substances” says: “In case the confirmatory test is found positive, the medical in charge of the organisation shall consult a medical review officer to determine if the result was due to a legitimate therapeutic treatment or some other innocuous source (for example pain relief medication containing codeine may trigger a positive result for opiates).Airlines try to create awareness and encourage employees to anonymously report addiction so that the same can be addressed. But mostly people avoid reporting the same, so this virtually remains a non-starter, said many officials. Officials running operations across airlines say the focus in India is primarily on self-reporting and de-addiction.“But given the easy availability of psychoactive substances, we need to make the consequences a bit tougher and act as deterrent. We have to increase random testing, that’s the only way out,” said an official. Under DGCA rules, all scheduled commercial airlines and air navigation service providers need to test at least 10% of their flight crew members and air traffic controllers every year.
Article Summary: Legal availability of marijuana for medicinal or recreational use in places like thailand and amsterdam has made life difficult for airlines flying there. Unlike simple breath analyser tests for checking if the crew is tipsy, the process of detecting consumption of psychoactive substances is difficult.

NEW DELHI: Arunachal Pradesh is indisputably an integral and inalienable part of India, govt asserted Tuesday in response to Beijing’s rejection of its decision to formally identify and map 27 places in the state. Following recent reports about fresh border tensions, govt also reiterated that “the state of border affairs will reflect on the state of larger bilateral ties”.The home ministry had last week identified 27 locations in Arunachal Pradesh by “standard place and feature names” on the official maps of Survey of India, saying this would facilitate their accurate recognition and better awareness among the public. Article Title: No Chinese encroachment in Arunachal, social media claims 'attention-seeking ploy': Report
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: There is no “slow encroachment” by China into Arunachal Pradesh, new agency ANI reported citing sources on Tuesday. The sources also rejected claims circulating on social media, describing them as “attention-seeking ploys” that lack specific evidence."There is no slow encroachment in Arunachal Pradesh by China as alleged," they said."Due to undemarcated border at times the patrols face off each other, this is resolved through existing mechanisms and protocols in vogue. The Army and ITBP are geared up to dominate the border, monitor and check Chinese activities. Sensational claims like this without going into specifics are attention-seeking ploys," the report said citing sources.They said China has historically laid claim to Arunachal Pradesh, referring to it as “South Tibet”. During the 1960 border talks, Beijing had claimed around 69,000 sq km of territory in the state.Also read | 'Arunachal is integral part of India, nothing can change this,' says MEA on China's fresh 'objections' ⁠"China has claims on Arunachal as South Tibet, articulated in 1960 border talks, wherein they claimed approx 69,000 sq km of the state territory. ⁠In 1959 China attacked the Assam Rifles outpost at Longju and captured it.The area has since been in adverse possession and is frequently in news due to infra development done in this area by China," they said."During 1962 India-China War, major Chinese operations were launched in Kameng, Subansiri, Siyom, Siang and Lohit valleys. However, after ceasefire the PLA went back North of the LAC. Arunachal Pradesh shares a large border with Tibet along Great Himalayan range. Concerted infra push in recent years has enabled enhanced ptlg and surveillance of the area," they added.The report comes after the ministry of external affairs (MEA) reiterated that Arunachal Pradesh is an "inalienable and integral part of India", referring to the recent "objection" by China over renaming places in the state."Let me reiterate this once again that Arunachal Pradesh is an inalienable and integral part of India and this is a fact that is self-evident. At the same time, let me also underline that nothing can change this indisputable reality," MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said.India officially identified 27 locations in Arunachal by their standard names on the survey of India map, countering China's repeated attempts to assign Chinese names to places in the state.
Article Summary: No'slow encroachment' by china in arunachal, report suggests, adding that the army and itbp are geared up to monitor and check chinese activities along the border. NEW DELHI: India is examining the implications of the recently signed Mecca pact between Saudi Arabia , Pakistan and Turkey from the perspective of national security and regional stability, the ministry of external affairs (MEA) said on Tuesday."The agreement that was signed recently. So, let me say that we continue to closely follow developments in the West Asia conflict. As far as this particular agreement is concerned, we are examining its implications, both from the perspective of our national security, as well as considerations of regional stability, peace and stability," MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said."India remains fully committed to meeting or safeguarding its national interests and will take all necessary measures in this regard," he added.Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey had signed the trilateral defence agreement last week, aimed at strengthening collective security amid continuing instability in West Asia linked to the conflict involving Iran.The agreement was signed following a joint defence summit attended by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.According to Pakistan's foreign ministry, the pact is based on the three countries' historical ties, shared strategic interests and longstanding defence cooperation. It includes a commitment that an armed attack against any one of the three countries would be regarded as an attack against all three.The agreement also seeks to strengthen collective deterrence and promote peace, security and stability in the region and beyond.

Article Title: Air India CEO meets MoCA, DGCA amid Phuket flight turbulence probe
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Air India's outgoing CEO reportedly met government officials on Tuesday amid the ongoing row after the Delhi-Phuket flight turbulence incident.The airlines' outgoing CEO Campbell Wilson met senior officials of MoCA and DGCA regarding the flight that suddenly lost about 300 feet of altitude last week, reported PTI, citing sources. The sources said the civil aviation ministry called the three senior airline executives for a meeting in the wake of the August 4 incident.Executive advisor to Tata Sons Chairman and former Civil Aviation Secretary Pradeep Singh Kharola as well as Air India's Head of Flight Safety Deepak Joshi also attended the meeting, they said.However, Reuters reported, citing sources that the civil aviation ​minister has ​summoned the CEO. No confirmation has come from the airlines or the government.Although, as Campbell was leaving, after meeting thesenior officials of MoCA and DGCA, he said, "We were just giving an update on the status of the investigation...It is up to him (MoCA Minister) to give an update."The meeting comes a day after the government advanced a probe into the incident, which involved the Airbus A320 suddenly losing about 300 feet of altitude during the flight.The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has classified the incident as serious and is examining the circumstances surrounding the sudden descent.The pilot-in-command is also under scrutiny after his psychoactive substance screening test on arrival was found to be “not negative”. The sample has been sent to a designated laboratory for confirmatory testing, with the final report awaited, the aviation ministry said.“Further action, as appropriate, will be taken based on the outcome of the investigation and confirmatory test results,” the ministry said.Under DGCA rules, a pilot whose initial screening is non-negative must be immediately removed from safety-sensitive duties until the confirmatory report is received. Both pilots of the August 4 Air India flight have been taken off flying duty pending the investigation.The AI 2379 flight was carrying 145 people from Phuket to Delhi when it suddenly lost altitude, injuring passengers and crew. The aircraft landed safely in Delhi, but 17 people were hospitalised.The AAIB probe is examining both possible mechanical issues and pilot behaviour. Investigators are also expected to analyse the aircraft's flight data and cockpit voice recorders to establish the sequence of events.
Article Summary: The airline's outgoing ceo wilson campbell is set to have met govt officials over the incident last week. No confirmation has come from the airlines or the government. Both pilots of the august 4 air india flight have been taken off flying duty pending the investigation.

Article Title: 3 Russian cosmonauts wave tricolour from Int’l Space Station to wish India on its 80th I-Day; recall decades-old Delhi-Moscow friendship
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: As India gears up to celebrate its 80th Independence Day on Aug 15, three Russian cosmonauts on board the International Space Station have extended their I-Day greetings to the Indian people by holding the tricolour and sending a special video message recalling decades-old friendship between Moscow and New Delhi. The message transmitted from the space station from an altitude of 408 km serves as a masterclass in orbital diplomacy.In the video message reposted by the Embassy of Russia in India on Monday, Russian space crew — Pyotr Dubrov, Anna Kikina and Andrey Fedyaev — congratulated India and described space exploration as a key pillar of bilateral ties. “Eight decades ago, India broke free from colonial rule and embarked on a journey towards self-reliance and prosperity... Dear friends, today the Republic of India is celebrating its 80th Independence Day,” cosmonaut Pyotr Dubrov said, extending his wishes to India.Holding the tricolour alongside three posters showcasing India-Russia space cooperation, the space crew highlighted key milestones in the Indo-Russian partnership, including the 1975 launch of India’s Aryabhata satellite and 1984 flight of India-born cosmonaut Rakesh Sharma.The cosmonauts also talked about India’s most-ambitious ongoing Gaganyaan programme, noting four Indian astronauts (Gaganauts) were trained in Russia — Prashanth Nair, Ajit Krishnan, Angad Pratap, and Shubhanshu Shukla completed their space training module at Russia's Yuri Gagarin Cosmonaut Training Centre in Star City between Feb 2020 and March 2021.Anna Kikina recalled Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin’s historic visit to India in Nov 1961. She quoted Gagarin’s famous words about the country: “India is very beautiful from above, but it is even more beautiful and special because it is home to true friends.”“The friendship between our countries has been time-tested, and space exploration is one of the main areas of our cooperation,” she said.
Article Summary: Three russian cosmonauts on board the international space station have extended their i-day greetings to the indian people. The message transmitted from the space station from an altitude of 408 km serves as a masterclass in orbital diplomacy. The space crew highlighted key milestones in the indo-russian partnership, including the 1975 launch of india’s aryabhata satellite.

"During the bi-weekly press briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that public discontent in PoK was answered with bullets and blackouts by authorities in Pakistan."We would like to highlight the human rights violations being committed in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir and other parts of the country. We call upon the international community to hold Pakistan accountable for its misdeeds, abuses and gross violations of human rights, including against its own people," Jaiswal said."Over the last several months, we have seen large-scale protests in PoK, including during and before the elections. Public discontent was answered with bullets, blackouts, repression and oppression. More than 90 people have been killed and many more injured. This has made news across the world," he added.Also Read | 'Arunachal is integral part of India, nothing can change this': MEA on China's fresh 'objections' The remarks came as at least 90 people, including protesters, security personnel and bystanders, were killed in clashes during June and July.The banned Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) has been staging protests in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) since June over the contentious 12 refugee seats. It has alleged that Pakistan's establishment manipulates these seats to install a prime minister of its choice to lead the so-called PoK government.Meanwhile, the third phase of elections in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) was held on Monday in four constituencies, amid violence and allegations of rigging. Polling started in Poonch Division’s Bagh and Haveli districts at 8 am, while elections in seven constituencies have been indefinitely postponed.Clashes between Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) and Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) workers were reported in some areas as the region's election commission classified most of the 803 polling stations as "sensitive or highly sensitive".After the first and second phases of polling, which were marred by violent protests and were held on July 27 and August 2, respectively, voting was scheduled for Monday in 11 constituencies of the Poonch Division in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir. There are 53 seats in the so-called PoK Legislative Assembly - 45 are directly elected, while eight are reserved for women, technocrats and clerics.The second phase of polling on August 2 was marred by violence and allegations of rigging. One person was killed and several others were injured.Also read | British national killed in PoK clashes; another held for over 2 months, says report The phase also included voting for the 12 refugee seats, which are at the centre of the ongoing controversy.Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) swept the second phase, winning 16 seats, while Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) secured the remaining five. In the first phase on July 27, PML-N won nine of the 13 seats, while PPP won four. With the first two phases combined, PML-N has already secured 24 seats.
Article Summary: Mea spokesperson randhir jaiswal said that public discontent in pok was answered with bullets and blackouts by authorities in pakistan. At least 90 people, including protesters, security personnel and bystanders, were killed in clashes during june and july.

Article Title: 'Arunachal is integral part of India, nothing can change this': MEA on China's fresh 'objections'
Article Text:
MEA asserted that 'nothing can change the fact Arunachal is part of India'

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Tuesday reiterated that Arunachal Pradesh is an “inalienable and integral part of India”, refering to the row with China over renaming places in the border state.“Let me reiterate this once again that Arunachal Pradesh is an inalienable and integral part of India and this is a fact that is self-evident. At the same time, let me also underline that nothing can change this indisputable reality,” the MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said in a media briefing.Separately, talking about India-China ties, the MEA spokesperson added, "In matters relating to the border areas between India and China, we have always emphasised in our discussions with the Chinese side that we consider these issues as most serious, and that maintaining peace and tranquillity in these areas is of the utmost importance. We have also stated that the state of our border affairs will reflect on the state of our larger bilateral ties. This was reiterated at the recently held 36th meeting of the WMCC on India-China border affairs. At this meeting, the two sides engaged in frank discussions and reviewed the situation along the Line of Actual Control. The Indian side once again underlined that maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas is essential for the overall development of bilateral relations."The remarks came after India formally identified 27 locations in Arunachal Pradesh by their standard names on the official Survey of India map, amid China's repeated attempts to assign Chinese names to places in the state.The government said the move is aimed at ensuring the accurate identification of the locations and improving public awareness of their geographical and historical significance.Also read: 'Discontent answered with bullets' - MEA slams Pakistan over PoK crackdown India has consistently rejected Beijing's practice of renaming places in Arunachal Pradesh, calling such attempts “vain and preposterous” and saying they cannot alter the fact that the state “was, is, and will” remain an integral part of India.Several of the 27 locations have strategic and historical significance, including Long Ju, the site of a 1959 India-China military confrontation, and Thag La, where one of the opening battles of the 1962 war took place. The list also includes Jairampur, an important logistics hub in eastern Arunachal Pradesh, as well as Jaswant Garh and the Sher-e-Thapa Memorial, which commemorate Indian military heroes of the 1962 war.Meanwhile, China issued multiple lists of names for places in Arunachal Pradesh, which it refers to as “Zangnan”. Beijing released its first list of six names in 2017, followed by 15 names in 2021 and 11 in 2023. New Delhi has rejected these names as “fictitious”, saying such attempts seek to create “baseless narratives” and cannot change the ground reality.
Article Summary: Mea asserted that 'nothing can change the fact arunachal is part of india' mea said maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas is of the utmost importance. China issued multiple lists of names for places in ar unachal pradesh, which it refers to as “zangnan”

Article Title: 'History will remember him kindly': Sonia Gandhi writes on Manmohan Singh after SC clean chit
Article Text:
Sonia hails former PM Manmohan Singh after SC clean chit

NEW DELHI: Days after the Supreme Court gave former prime minister Manmohan Singh a clean chit in the coal block allocation case, senior Congress leader Sonia Gandhi on Tuesday invoked former PM's legacy and attacked the Narendra Modi government.Sonia said Singh's record of integrity and accountability was in stark contrast to the way the Modi government has functioned. She said history would remember Singh as a quiet, gentle but "highly consequential prime minister."Taking a dig at Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Sonia said that since he is currently "forgiving" students who attacked him, he could also use the opportunity to forgive himself for his "undignified slander" against Singh.The Congress parliamentary party chairperson said the Supreme Court judgment ended what she described as one of the most tragic episodes in public discourse -- the "witch-hunt against Dr Singh, a man of the most remarkable probity and integrity.""The lobby against him was coordinated and well-organised, with actors stretching from the bureaucracy to the media, the judiciary, civil society, and most certainly to the RSS and BJP.Today, their bogus crusade has come to its inevitable conclusion of nothingness. Dr Singh has been vindicated on every count," Sonia said in an article published in The Indian Express.Also read: Coal block scam case in Supreme Court: Ex-PM Manmohan Singh gets clean chit two years after his death Sonia said July 29, 2026, was an important but largely unacknowledged date in India's recent political history. On that day, the Supreme Court upheld the CBI's clean chit to Singh in the alleged coal block allocation scam.She also pointed out that the Supreme Court criticised the trial court for rejecting the CBI's closure reports and making adverse remarks against Singh without any "compelling reason".Sonia said Singh's record of integrity and accountability stood in contrast to what she called as the Modi government's "misuse of agencies" such as the Enforcement Directorate (ED) and the CBI."Its purpose has been to exert pressure on politicians. Leaders are either silenced through coercion or cynically folded into the BJP or, in some remarkable instances, rewarded with ministerial positions as well."When credible accusations of corruption emerge, the Modi government simply brushes them aside. Corrupt when you're in the Opposition, suddenly clean when you jump ship!" Sonia said.Sonia also said it was not a coincidence that Modi was among the most vocal critics of Singh."His snide and atrocious remarks in the Rajya Sabha on February 8, 2017, that only Dr Singh knew 'the art of bathing with a raincoat on', will go down as the lowest point of our parliamentary history," former Congress president said."Introspection, like charity, must begin from home. Ultimately, the attack on Dr Singh was motivated by a desperate desire to shift the public conversation and narrative away from his outstanding governance record," she added.Sonia highlighted Singh's economic record, saying his government brought major economic changes, high growth rates and a rise in consumption and private investment.She said India also showed resilience during the 2008 global financial crisis."Let us not forget that in spite of the reworking of how the growth of India's GDP is calculated, the 10 years of the UPA government saw higher economic growth than the past 12 years, resulting in millions being pulled out of poverty," Sonia said.She also highlighted several welfare and social justice initiatives introduced during Singh's tenure.According to Sonia, the Manmohan Singh government delivered the constitutional promise of the Right to Education and expanded OBC reservation in centrally funded higher education institutions, including the IITs and IIMs."The Forest Rights Act recognised the ancestral rights of our Adivasi and forest-dwelling communities, after a decades-long struggle. The MGNREGA, recently demolished by the Modi government, was the most powerful social security intervention set up anywhere," she said.Sonia also cited the National Food Security Act, 2013, as another major achievement of Singh's government. The law guaranteed access to basic food rations for crores of families.She said civil society became stronger during Singh's tenure and people could protest against the government and prime minister.Sonia also claimed that Singh regularly remained accountable to Parliament and the media through more than 100 unscripted press conferences."And of course, we cannot forget that the landmark and path-breaking Indo-US nuclear deal, which overturned decades of nuclear discrimination against and denial towards India and marked our arrival on the global stage, was possible because of his political courage and sustained initiative," she said.Sonia said the allegations against Singh's integrity had now been exposed as baseless and that his record was increasingly being recognised as a period of economic, political and social progress."We all certainly regret that he is not here to see this day and to guide the nation with his wisdom. But it is a solace to us all that his prophetic prediction of January 2014 is becoming increasingly self-evident with every passing day."History will indeed remember him kindly as a quiet, gentle but a most consequential prime minister," Sonia said.Her remarks came after the Supreme Court closed the criminal case against Singh by setting aside a summoning order against him.Singh, who died on December 27, 2024, now stands formally acquitted in the high-profile criminal case.
Article Summary: Sonia hails former pm manmohan singh after sc clean chit in coal block allocation case. She said history would remember singh as a quiet, gentle but "highly consequential prime minister" sonia said it was not a coincidence that modi was among the most vocal critics of singh.

NEW DELHI: Discussion on the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2011 (FCRA) 2026, did not figure Monday in the business advisory committee (BAC) deliberations involving govt and different parties over Lok Sabha’s agenda for the remaining three days of the monsoon session, deepening uncertainty over whether the governing alliance will push for passage of the contentious legislation.Govt is said to have reached out to the Congress-led opposition seeking its views on referring the FCRA bill to a joint committee of Parliament for scrutiny.Sources said Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla spoke with Congress member of Parliament KC Venugopal regarding the govt’s proposal, but he instead sought complete withdrawal of the legislation.Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill was introduced on March 25 in Lok Sabha’s last session but has not been taken up for discussion yet amid sharp protests from opposition parties and minority groups, especially Christian bodies.Govt sources said they are looking at allaying their concerns, insisting that the apprehensions of Christian groups are ill-founded as the bill is religion-neutral. “Moreover, they receive less than 17% of funding under FCRA. But complaints have primarily come from them. We are sure about our bill but will reach out to critics,” a minister said.With opposition protesting in Parliament over a host of issues, a discussion on the bill is all but ruled out, denying govt an opportunity to address the criticism.
